business_scope.primary_industry_name: Maritime Seafarer Staffing and Vessel Crew Management Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France's comprehensive network of over 100 bilateral investment treaties (BITs), including France–Germany (1959), France–Argentina (1991), France–China (2007), France–USA (1966), all still in force or replaced by EU-level instruments
France's double taxation agreement network of more than 80 DTAAs, including France–China DTA (2013), France–USA DTA (2019), France–Great Britain DTA (2008, amended 2019)

L561-1 to L562-10) as amended by the transposition of EU Directive 2015/849 and Directive 2018/843; Code de commerce (Art. L156-1 to L156-3) on beneficial ownership declarations; Décret n° 2016-1635 of 2 December 2016; Arrêté of 15 January 2015 establishing the AML/CFT threshold; Position-Regulation of the AMF (General Regulation, Art. 321-1 et seq.) for investment services; Bank of France (ACPR) guidelines to integrate fundraising and sanctions compliance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or consular officer in the shareholder's country of origin / sworn translator for French language version
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (if issuing state is not party to the Hague Convention) followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed credit institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (as above) plus sworn French translation if not already in French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and Certificate of good standing (or recent extract from the business register) for any foreign corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or chamber of commerce in the foreign corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention member) OR Consular Legalization at the French Embassy/Consulate (non-member state) plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (solvency and conduct) for each foreign shareholder and UBO, issued in the last 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution in the country of residence or incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract or equivalent certificate of non-conviction for directors, senior managers, and UBOs (including for matters relevant to maritime labour and transport security)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial authority in the country of nationality or previous residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Written informed consent document for the nomination of the French legal representative (Président) of the SAS, signed by the foreign individual or corporate president
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAS President, if resident outside France, signed before a notary or consular officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (if appliable) plus sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening against: (1) EU Council consolidated sanctions lists (including UN Security Council sanctions, Egmont Group, and France's own national lists), (2) OFAC SDN list for all USD foreign compliance, (3) Bank of France / ACPR recommended high-risk countries (FATF blacklists/grey zones), (4) French 'GELI' (Gouvernement, Endettement, Litige) and 'FIBA' (Fichage à travers le Conseil d'État) for potential judicial prohibitions, (5) national French PEP lists (Trimagan) and beneficial ownership registries of French departments, (6) Politically Exposed Person status must be scrutinized for all shareholders, UBOs, and the appointed President in conformity with CNIL-approved protocols; enhanced due diligence is triggered on any positive result.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) — online portal at registre-national-entreprises.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Article L123-1 of the French Commercial Code imposes that constitutional documents are in French; the corporate name must be written in Latin script with diacritics if necessary. If a foreign language trademark is adopted as the company name, a French transliteration or an accepted French-language equivalent must be provided for RNE indexing. The name must not be confusingly similar to a widely known trademark, may not be contrary to public order/bonnes moeurs, and must be composed of freely invented terms; use of 'France' or 'République' is strictly limited and harmless use only.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection issued by INPI’s RNE is a first-cycle administrative denial. The applicant may submit a written rectification request through the same portal, reference the refusal and propose a revised name. If the rejection remains, the applicant may initiate an administrative complaint before the coordinating director of INPI within 2 months of the rejection notification. If refused again, a judicial appeal lies before the nearest commercial court (Tribunal Judiciaire/Commercial Chamber) in the applicant’s electoral district. The procedure prescribes no right to extension of the 30-day reservation period; when rejection occurs, the reservation is automatically expired and a new search must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office (bureau en domiciliation) is generally permissible for the registered office of a French SAS, subject to the provision of a statutory domiciliation contract and compliance with the 'Option 4' domiciliation rules under Article L123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code. However, for the maritime crew recruitment agency scope (ISIC 5222), the French Directorate of Maritime Affairs (Direction des Affaires Maritimes) will, in the exercise of its licensing power for 'recruitment and placement of seafarers', typically require demonstrable physical operational presence in France, including an office suite for seafarer interviews and document handling. Therefore, virtual office status is only recommendable as a temporary initial seat, not as a permanent substantive presence for the licensed activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified 72% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 18 months of operation. The French maritime administration (Direction des Affaires Maritimes, DPMTM) and the Social Investigations Unit (CISS) have a mandate for on-site checks at crew manning offices to verify seafarer contracts, compliance with maritime employment standards, and proper record‑keeping. The likelihood is elevated for newly licensed agencies and is considered 'high risk'.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative tariff as published in INPI’s fee schedule (décision du Director Général)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAS drafting of articles of incorporation and closing covenant (Le Statut de la Société)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Eligible legal counsel/attorney at the Paris or Marseille bar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SAS corporate setup, subject to legal fee schedule of the bar association (unregulated above minimum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the mandatory incorporation notice in a SHAL (legal gazette)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated SHAL (Support d’Annonces Légales, local press authorized)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Gazette’s own statutory/per-page tariff, benchmarked between EUR 150 and EUR 220

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation of all foreign-certified notarization/apostilled documents (typically 5 documents, approximately 750 words)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-appointed sworn translator (Traducteur Expert près de la Cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-word or per-page rates, average EUR 55/page; market benchmark EUR 450–650

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille processing fees in the country of origin for UBO/shareholder documents (5 documents, per state fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Apostille authority in each foreign country (e.g., Secretary of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Varied foreign state tariffs, average USD 25–30 per apostille; no French government fee applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization fee for any document from a non-Hague Convention state (contingency, estimated 3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French Embassy or Consulate in the issuing country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: French consular fee schedule (Décret n°2009-974), per document fee varies EUR 20–40

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RNE / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce registration fee (QMR + DMR + RCS + statutory UBO registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Court Registry) / French State RNE
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff (Taxe de création SAS), approximately EUR 70–80

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC and beneficial ownership due-diligence provider (full background screening, PEP watch-lists, corporate chain-of-ownership analysis)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for comprehensive UBO piercing per company; reduced for a single-UBO setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional opinion on foreign shareholder capacity and the enforcement of the nominee clause (Président non-résident) under French law
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark hourly rate or fixed fee for due-diligence advice in cross-border corporate setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-licensing administrative review fee for the maritime crew recruitment authorization (Autorisation préfectorale de recrutement et de la fourniture des gens de mer)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Direction Interrégionale de la Mer (DIRM) / Préfecture de région
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative fee published in the Official Journal for maritime service licensing (typically EUR 150–180)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 227-1 through L. 227-30 and L. 210-1 through L. 210-10; applicable provisions of Decree No. 2023-908 (filing procedures) and Code des transports Articles L. 5341-1 et seq. for maritime crew placement services.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier unique de formalité d'entreprise (M0 / RCS constitution declaration) filed exclusively via the electronic Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SAS has no statutory minimum capital under French law; however, share subscription must be in full and paid in at least 1 EUR per share. Funds may be held in escrow or a blocked bank account until the company is duly registered and the RCS certificate has been issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The incorporation of the SAS under the name, form, and articles of association presented is unanimously ratified. Each shareholder shall subscribe and pay in full the shares recorded in the capital subscription schedule. The registered office is fixed at the address indicated in the articles of association, and the President and any Directors are hereby appointed as officers with full powers to act. The appointed representatives are authorized to complete all commercial registry filings, legal publications, and banking obligations and to execute any additional document necessary for registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association and Depository of Initial Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or private written deed; bank or qualified escrow depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the SAS statuts containing the corporate name, registered office, duration, share capital, share classes, management powers, decision-making procedures, and object clause specifically covering maritime crew recruitment. If capital is paid in cash, deposit the funds in a French bank blocked account or with an authorized notarial escrow. Hold the execution minute and capital deposit certificate for filing.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (statuts constitutifs)
Capital subscription and payment certificate (attestation de blocage des fonds or notary's receipt)
Identity documents and proof of address of each shareholder and officer
Company name availability certificate or negative keyword check
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defect in the statuts or capital certificate identified by the registry and re-submit the amended document through the Guichet Unique; a notary may re-issue an attestation if the deposit structure is challenged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Company Formation Announcement in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal announcement journal (journal d'annonces légales - JAL) in the department where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place a mandatory legal announcement containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office address, object, and the corporate SIREN registration pending application. Obtain the certificate of publication (attestation de parution) for attachment to the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Completed announcement text
Proof of payment of publication fee
Company project identification (name and address only)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed text is rejected for missing mandatory clauses, adapt the announcement to the statement from the JAL and republish an amended notice; the certificate is issued only after final publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Guichet Unique and INSEE/RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique for transmission to the RCS (Registre du commerce et des sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and complete the 'Création d'activité – société' dossier. Attach the signed statuts, publication certificate, capital deposit proof, identity of the beneficial owner declaration, and the declaration of no incompatibility of executives. The system transmits the dossier to the RCS of the chosen registered office's commercial court.
required_dossiers: M0 / electronic registration form completed in French
Signed Articles of Association (statuts)
Legal publication certificate (attestation de parution)
Capital deposit certificate (attestation de blocage des fonds)
Beneficial owner declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
Declaration of non-conviction and compatibility for legal representatives
Proof of company domiciliation (lease, accommodation, or sublease)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond within 15 days via the Guichet Unique electronic portal; the RCS examiner will suspend the procedure until all missing information or corrections are provided. Re-file the corrected attachment and request priority replay if the statutory timeframe is exceeded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Registration Certificate and Completion of Post-Registration Legalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Greffe du Tribunal de commerce and INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the RCS delivers an extract Kbis and assigns a SIREN/SIRET registration number. Use the Kbis as the company's first legal identity for opening banks, obtaining a company seal, and registering with the social and tax authorities via the same portal.
required_dossiers: Kbis certificate French extract (provided by the registry)
SIREN/SIRET confirmation letter
Company domiciliation proof
Executive judicial records excerpt (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis or SIREN detail is erroneous, file a correction request with the relevant RCS greffe through the Guichet Unique or directly using the rectification form; temporary working registration can be requested for immediate commercial opening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Maritime Seafarer Crew Recruitment Agency Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de la Mer — Direction Générale des Affaires Maritimes, de la Pêche et de l'Aquaculture (DGAMPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a specific license application after RCS registration for the placement of seafarer services. Provide evidence of professional fitness, compliance with international maritime labor laws, financial solvency, and the operational protocol for crew recruitment, placement, and payroll. Obtain the formal agrément before commercial commencement of ship crew staffing activities.
required_dossiers: Kbis and SIREN certificate
Completed license application form for crew placement agency
Business plan and financial capacity evidence
List of operations to be carried out
Compliance statement with ILO Maritime Labour Convention and International Safety Management requirements
Criminal record extract for executives
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGAMPA refuses the agrément, appeal through the administrative court within two months; rectify identified compliance gaps and resubmit an application for a new review with a complete evidential file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Health, Fire Safety, and Workplace Licensing Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CARSAT (regional occupational health and safety body) and municipal fire commission (commissions de sécurité)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For office premises, register the facility with the building manager and prefecture, obtain a fire safety classification for environments open to employees, ensure staff first-aid training, and complete an occupancy approval if the building falls under category 4 or 5 of the Fire Safety Code. For maritime crew, implement any additional physical safety regulations related to dispatch areas.
required_dossiers: Building compliance and structural safety certificate
Fire extinguisher inspection reports
Staff workstation registration documents
Project of occupancy if required by local planning law
Company's occupational risk assessment document
Electrical installation certificate (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Subject to a deficiency notice, carry out the required remedial measures and request a re-inspection by the fire prevention authority; if CARSAT rejects the workplace clearance, update the risk assessment and resubmit after completing corrective actions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Affaires Maritimes, de la Pêche et de l'Aquaculture (DGAMPA) at the French Ministry of Maritime Affairs
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément d'agence de placement de gens de mer (Seafarer Recruitment Agency License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique — Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (non-ICPE service activity; no mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment required for an administrative and crew dispatch office)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to a service-only agency; if a small workshop or storage area exists, must comply with municipal wastewater discharge limits and sorted waste management obligations under Articles L. 541-1 et seq., including mandatory separate collection of plastic, paper, and hazardous waste and prohibition of uncontrolled discharge into drains.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspections must be obtained from the local fire safety/prevention commission for the office premises; if the office is located in a building open to the public, an access to work certificate is required. In all cases, the employer must obtain a workplace clearance from CARSAT and perform risk assessments for repeated movements and visual ergonomics, and fire drill records must be retained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS obtain SIREN automatically upon registration at greffe du tribunal de commerce; VAT ID is FR + SIREN. Foreign entities register for tax ID through guichet-entreprises.fr or equivalent procedures for French establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available in France; entities are subject to mandatory entity-level corporate taxation. Hybrid mismatch provisions under EU ATAD directive apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturation électronique for B2B since October 2024 via PEPPOL; real-time fiscal clearance with digital stamping and API integration required for compliant transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the EU are zero-rated for VAT with proof of dispatch. Services provided to non-EU customers are zero-rated if performed outside France and invoiced to non-EU entity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties for fraudulent export zero-rating claims include up to 80% of evaded tax plus interest; retrospective clawback and potential criminal sanctions under French tax code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank framework; foreign-exchange and balance-of-payments reporting is supplemented by the French Treasury Directorate-General (Direction générale du Trésor), the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR), and applicable European Union regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies a liberal foreign-exchange regime. The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax, customs, and statistical-reporting requirements. A French SAS may generally receive foreign capital, pay foreign suppliers, remit dividends, repay shareholder loans, and transfer profits abroad without a general central-bank approval or mandatory conversion into euros. Profit distributions remain subject to French corporate-law requirements, including approval of annual accounts, availability of distributable reserves, preservation of share capital, and applicable withholding-tax, treaty, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse rules. Banks may require evidence of the underlying transaction, source of funds, tax residence, ultimate beneficial ownership, corporate approvals, and compliance with sanctions screening. Foreign direct investment screening may apply to a non-EU investment in a sensitive French sector; ordinary maritime crew recruitment and staffing activities are not automatically within a sensitive sector, but the precise activity, technology, data, defense, port, or critical-infrastructure exposure must be reviewed before closing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no mandatory export-receipt conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency receipts into euros. Export receipts may remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's discretion, subject to bank documentation, sanctions controls, tax accounting, customs evidence, and applicable Banque de France or European statistical reporting. Banks may request invoices, contracts, bills of lading, crew-management agreements, customer identification, and proof of services for compliance and transaction-monitoring purposes. Any reporting obligation is transaction- or institution-specific and should not be confused with a currency-surrender rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Groupe BPCE, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne network banks

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment accounts, foreign-currency collections, payroll disbursements, and low-to-medium-volume cross-border transfers; low as a complete substitute for a French relationship bank where the SAS requires capital deposit certification, domestic credit facilities, commercial letters of credit, maritime-sector underwriting, or complex trade documentation. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to French customers unless it is authorised in the European Economic Area or operates through a valid passporting or local-authorisation arrangement. The provider must be an authorised electronic-money institution, payment institution, bank, or permitted agent. Client-money safeguarding, AML/KYC, sanctions screening, PSD2 requirements, operational-resilience rules, data-protection obligations, transaction limits, correspondent-bank dependencies, and account-closure risk must be assessed. An EMI account should not be represented as a French bank deposit account unless the provider is a licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all SAS directors appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified or reliable electronic identification, video identification, certified corporate documents, and verified beneficial-owner information. The bank may nevertheless require a physical meeting, live video interview, French or EU-resident signatory, notarised or apostilled documents, specimen signatures, or in-person verification based on risk, ownership complexity, non-resident management, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual payment flows, maritime-sector counterparties, or inability to independently verify documents. Capital-deposit accounts are subject to the selected bank's acceptance procedures and generally require satisfactory identification before issuance of the deposit certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or multi-layered ownership structure, nominee shareholders, unexplained holding companies, or inability to identify every ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; certificate of incorporation and registry extract; complete ownership chart to natural persons; beneficial-owner declaration; passports and residential-address evidence for directors, signatories, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners; board or shareholder resolutions; explanation of the ownership rationale; tax-residence information; and certified translations where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital, shareholder loans, or subsequent capital injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements showing accumulation of funds; audited or management accounts; shareholder net-worth and funding declaration; executed capital-increase or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; transfer instructions identifying the remitter; tax filings or financial statements; and evidence that the remitting account is controlled by the disclosed investor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ship-crew recruitment or vessel-management activity not supported by a coherent licensing and operating profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; French registration evidence; employment and crewing-service agreements; shipowner and vessel-counterparty list; evidence of applicable maritime recruitment or placement authorisations; seafarer-protection and employment-compliance procedures; insurance certificates; office and personnel evidence; and explanation of whether the company acts as agent, employer, payroll processor, or subcontractor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned countries, sanctioned shipowners, vessels, ports, beneficial owners, or maritime counterparties with adverse media.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty and vessel due-diligence file; IMO numbers; flag-state and ownership records; sanctions-screening reports; beneficial-owner certifications; contractual sanctions clauses; cargo and route information; payment-purpose evidence; escalation and approval records; and documented refusal or blocking controls for prohibited transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of cross-border payroll payments to seafarers in multiple jurisdictions with inconsistent names, beneficiary accounts, or payment narratives.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Crew roster; verified identity documents; employment contracts; payroll registers; timesheets or vessel assignments; wage calculations; beneficiary-bank validation; payment authorization matrix; reconciliation reports; tax and social-security treatment analysis; and documented controls for duplicate, amended, returned, or third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or repetitive incoming payments that do not match declared revenue, invoices, or contractual cash-flow expectations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer contracts; invoices; remittance advice; service-delivery evidence; vessel and crew records; accounts receivable ledger; expected-volume forecast; management explanation of seasonal or project-driven flows; VAT and accounting records; and transaction-level reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, cash-intensive settlement, third-party funding, cryptoasset proceeds, or unexplained pass-through transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal prohibition in treasury policy; documented payment-routing rules; bank statements; third-party payment approvals; source-of-funds evidence; commercial rationale; enhanced due-diligence report; and remediation evidence showing that future receipts and payments will use accounts held in the SAS's legal name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent corporate data across the French commercial registry, tax records, bank application, beneficial-owner register, website, and contracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Single controlled corporate-data pack; updated registry extract; amended articles or management appointment documents; tax-registration evidence; written discrepancy explanation; certified translations; and confirmation from the legal representative that all submitted information is current and complete.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential permanent-establishment, payroll, employment, or regulatory exposure created by foreign offices, local agents, or crew personnel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-by-country operating map; intercompany and agency agreements; foreign registrations; payroll and employer analysis; tax advice; employment-law assessment; transfer-pricing support; delegated-authority schedule; and description of where services are performed and where personnel are managed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to satisfy ongoing transaction-monitoring, record-retention, or suspicious-transaction escalation requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CTF policy; sanctions policy; customer-risk classification; payment approval workflow; staff training records; monitoring scenarios; alert investigation files; escalation procedures to the compliance officer; retention schedule; independent testing; and documented reporting procedures to TRACFIN where legally required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital to an account held in the exact legal name of the French SAS through a regulated bank or authorised payment institution. For formation capital, use the selected bank's capital-deposit account and obtain the deposit certificate required for registration; release funds to the operational account after incorporation and satisfaction of the bank's conditions. For a subsequent equity injection, use a documented capital increase, share-premium contribution, or other legally characterised contribution approved by the competent corporate body. For shareholder debt, execute a written loan agreement and classify the transfer consistently in the accounting records. Use SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 through a regulated correspondent chain, with the correct ordering customer, beneficiary, ultimate beneficial owner where required, and transparent payment narrative. France has no universal FX purpose-code regime for ordinary capital transfers; identify the transfer as equity contribution, share premium, shareholder loan, or other legally accurate purpose and provide the corporate resolution, investment agreement, source-of-funds evidence, remitter ownership evidence, and tax documentation requested by the receiving bank. Verify receipt against the sending-bank confirmation, reconcile bank charges and FX conversion, and retain records for AML, accounting, tax, and statistical-reporting purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area; use SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 cross-border payment messages for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. For supplier, shipowner, and crewing-service settlements, retain the underlying contract, invoice, purchase order, vessel or crew reference, beneficiary verification, sanctions-screening result, and payment approval. Commercial letters of credit may be issued, advised, confirmed, amended, or settled through the banking network using documentary-credit messaging, including SWIFT MT700 for issuance and applicable presentation, amendment, and settlement messages; the bank will apply the governing UCP 600 terms where incorporated and may require collateral or credit capacity. Documentary collections, open-account payments, bank guarantees, and prepayment may be used subject to counterparty, sanctions, fraud, and trade-document controls. Payroll payments should be made from the SAS account using validated beneficiary data, documented employment or service records, and a controlled multi-approval process. Apply EU and French sanctions, AML, tax, employment, VAT, and accounting requirements to every payment; do not split transactions to avoid bank controls or reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorised bank or regulated investment firm, supported by an identifiable underlying exposure, documented hedge purpose, approved counterparty limit, maturity schedule, valuation, collateral terms where applicable, and accounting treatment.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps with an authorised bank or regulated investment firm for documented funding, liquidity, or currency-mismatch management, subject to counterparty credit limits, EMIR obligations where applicable, confirmation, collateral, valuation, and reporting requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards may be used for currencies subject to local non-deliverability or settlement restrictions, provided the instrument is legally available in the relevant currency, entered into with an authorised counterparty, and supported by documented exposure, ISDA or equivalent terms, EMIR compliance, and applicable market-conduct controls.

Foreign-exchange options and collars may be used for hedging identifiable receivables, payables, payroll, or funding exposures, subject to suitability, governance, premium and valuation controls, and the applicable MiFID II, EMIR, accounting, and disclosure requirements.

Spot foreign-exchange conversions through regulated banks or payment institutions for ordinary operational settlement; maintain a written treasury policy distinguishing hedging from speculative trading and prohibiting unapproved leveraged or naked positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (bilan, compte de résultat, annexes) and shareholder approval record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) via Infogreffe / INPI Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the shareholders' approval of accounts and in all cases no later than 6 months after fiscal year end (unless a court-ordered extension is granted)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generates administrative delay penalties (EUR 1,500 base, EUR 4,000 if repeated), possible daily court fine (astreinte), personal criminal fine up to EUR 9,000 for the legal representative; after formal notice, continued omission can lead to RCS strike-off (radiation) and termination of the legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of company data (déclaration annuelle de l'entreprise / mise à jour du RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) through the INPI Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every year before the anniversary of RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file suspends issuance of up-to-date Kbis extracts and may trigger a formal notice followed by administrative strike-off from the RCS if not regularised.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration annuelle de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) via INPI Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary date of the company's RCS registration or of the last recorded UBO declaration, and within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inaccurate filing exposes the legal representative to up to 6 months' imprisonment and EUR 7,500 fine (legal entity: EUR 37,500), plus possible judicial fine and suspension of corporate rights; continued default can be treated as a breach of statutory books requirements and support strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a French SAS when, at fiscal year-end, at least two of the three thresholds are exceeded: balance sheet total EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (excl. VAT) EUR 8,000,000; average permanent employees 50. Audit is also required for any SAS controlling or controlled by other entities that is itself required to prepare consolidated financial statements, or if ordered by court.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory financial statements must be prepared under French GAAP (plan comptable général per ANC Regulation 2014-03); IFRS is permitted at the option of the group (not the SAS alone) only for consolidated financial statements, not for the company's individual annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, on the anniversary of the RCS registration (and again within 30 days after any shareholding transfer affecting beneficial ownership), the SAS's legal representative must file the updated beneficial-owner declaration using the RBE form through the Guichet unique/Infogreffe. The declaration must identify each ultimate owner who directly or indirectly holds more than 25% of capital or voting rights or controls the company; failure to confirm is enforced as a criminal offence and exposes the company to sanctions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate for qualifying small enterprises on first €42,500 of taxable profit; Research Tax Credit (CIR) and Innovation Tax Credit (CII); participation exemption on qualified share disposals; group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale); loss carryforward indefinitely with annual cap of €1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding €1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n° 2065 (Cerfa n° 11632) with annexes 2050–2067; filed electronically via EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatisés) or GEDI portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year fiscal periods: file by the second business day following 1 May; for non-calendar year-ends: within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1a — Net profit for the fiscal period (Bénéfice net)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the net accounting profit adjusted for tax deductions and reintegrations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company with a French permanent establishment: enter only PE-attributable profit; otherwise leave nil and attach Schedule 2065 if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying portion of taxable profit eligible for the reduced rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Eligible only where the French PE qualifies as a small entity under French law; provide substantiating turnover and asset declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3a — Tax losses offset (Report en avant)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses offset against current-year taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may only offset losses attributable to the French PE; ensure defensive documentation supports the loss origin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate tax credits (including CIR, CII, foreign tax credits) to be imputed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State credits duly allocable to French-source income; non-residents must attach Schedule 2069-RCI and foundations of credit entitlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% increase in gross tax liability where no formal notice was issued (or 5% if paid within 30 days); a 40% penalty for failure to file within 30 days after a formal notice, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% monthly. Missing schedules or incorrectly completed boxes can incur a €150 per omission fine up to €10,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Article 119 bis CGI on distributions to non-resident legal entities; generally 0% for EU corporate shareholders holding ≥10% for 2 years under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must submit a valid residence certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority to the French withholding agent before, or at the time of, payment to obtain reduced treaty withholding; where overpaid, a refund claim must be filed on Form 5001 with the French competent authority within the statutory period. The French entity must maintain an avis de situation fiscale and proof of EU holding for directive relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding at 33⅓% under Article 182 B CGI (final tax for non-residents without a French PE); treaty rates generally 10% (or 0% for copyright royalties in some DTAs). Interest: no domestic withholding on ordinary arm's-length interest; 25% WHT may apply for revenue-sharing loans or if recharacterized as a distribution; treaty rates generally 0% for arm's-length interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million annual net turnover or gross fixed assets for the French entity triggering Local File obligation; EUR 750 million consolidated group revenue for Master File obligation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; however, the general abuse-of-law doctrine (Article L.64 of the Book of Tax Procedures) and anti-fragmentation rules require actual business substance, fixed place of business, and management control. A company organized purely for treaty-shopping or tax avoidance will be re-characterized with severe penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable revenue, overstating deductions, hiding cash receipts, or concealing offshore profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to €75,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (increased to €100,000 and 7 years for aggravated fraud, organised gang, or concealment); civil tax penalty of 80% of the evaded tax plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted personally, subject to travel bans, asset seizure, and disqualification; where the corporate veil is pierced, they face civil restitution for the tax deficiency and damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain or submit the Local File/Master File, or knowingly entering into non-arm's-length intercompany transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative adjustment with a 5% fine on the reassessed transfer-pricing adjustment (capped at €100,000) for missing documentation; 40% negligence penalty or 80% concealment penalty plus 0.20% monthly interest on the tax re-assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve artificial pricing may be subject to criminal conspiracy charges, personal fines, and civil liability; travel bans and seizure of assets may be imposed where fraud is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Lack of Economic Substance / Tax Abuse (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or using an artificial French structure with no real staff, premises, business management, or operational substance solely to circumvent tax or obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization of the arrangement under Article L.64 with an 80% penalty; the arrangement may be set aside and taxes recalculated; in criminal cases, up to €50,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment for abuse in fraudulent intent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly and severally liable for the tax consequences, and may be subject to criminal sanctions, personal bankruptcy, travel restrictions, and management disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, failure to declare suspicious crew payroll transactions, or misuse of wire/payroll rails for laundering illegal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines by ACPR up to €5 million or, if greater, twice the benefit derived; criminal penalties under the Monetary and Financial Code: up to 5 years' imprisonment and €375,000 fine for natural persons, and up to €1 million fine for legal persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal prosecution, personal fines, asset seizure, travel bans, and prohibition from managing financial institutions; civil liability for damages to third parties.
